title: Implicit Values Embedded in How Humans and LLMs Complete Subjective Everyday Tasks
findings: LLMs' handling of religious content significantly differed from humans. In a fund distribution task, humans were much more likely to distribute funds to religious organizations proportionally to local demographics than any LLM. When editing an email with a religious quote, GPT and Llama models almost always retained it, Gemini 1.5 never did, and Claude 3's behavior varied starkly depending on the specific religion of the quote, while humans retained it about half the time. LLMs, unlike humans, never prioritized a person's religious contributions when creating a summary of their achievements. LLMs also tended to prioritize emails about church fundraisers more highly than humans did.
